tags.notes: First-magnitude spring complex on the Santa Fe River, privately operated day-use site. Devil's Eye/Devil's Ear/Little Devil vents connect to an extensive mapped cave system (~30,000 ft of conduits); cavern zone is Intermediate, full cave system requires full cave certification. Individual vent coordinates not separately published.

Collapsed sinkhole/karst window opening into a large partly-submerged cavern; widely used for open-water and cavern training. Site of a significant 1960 Pleistocene fossil excavation (47+ mammal species). Entry is via stairs into the sinkhole, not a typical beach/dock shore entry.
Sinkhole with wide open basin leading to a large cavern chamber; widely used for open-water and cavern training. ~100 ft visibility typical.

name: Wes Skiles Peacock Springs State Park

tags.notes: State park protecting one of the longest interconnected underwater cave systems in the continental US (Peacock I/II/III + Orange Grove Sink). Total mapped-passage length cited inconsistently across sources (~33,000 ft vs 38,000+ ft) - flagged as unresolved. Full cave penetration restricted to full-cave-certified divers; individual sink entrances not separately geolocated.

Spring basin on the Withlacoochee River leading to an extensive mapped cave system (nearly 8 miles of surveyed passage per one source); entrance/shallow zone ~60-70ft, deeper system exceeds 100ft and reaches ~145ft in farthest surveyed sections.

IMPORTANT ACCESS FLAG: Florida State Parks permits open-water scuba diving ONLY here - cave entry and dive lights are explicitly prohibited, unlike most other sites in this list. Home to the wreck of the Confederate steamboat Madison, scuttled 1863.

Suwannee County park; cave system extends 1,200+ ft via a steep 'chimney' formation to ~100 ft depth. Coordinates from a locator directory, not independently cross-verified against a second precise source - treat as approximate.

Florida's first state park (1968); first-magnitude spring with multiple karst openings (Headspring, Catfish Hotel, Sue Sink, Friedman's Sink). Cave diving permitted for certified cave divers with depth/lighting restrictions. Main spring run closed to swimmers in winter for manatee protection - manatees seasonally present, not guaranteed.

Panhandle location (Holmes County) - outside the core north-central FL springs belt. Large basin with shallow training platforms (20ft); cave passage beyond the cavern is barred by a security gate at ~115ft for diver safety after multiple documented fatalities - full cave certification required for any attempt beyond the cavern zone.

Panhandle location (Jackson County) - outside the core north-central FL springs belt. Feeds Merritt's Mill Pond; full cave certification required. Closed to divers in summer months for recreational swimmer access. Coordinate from a single spring-locator source, not independently cross-verified.

Morrison Springs County Park, Ponce de Leon, Walton County. Open basin bottoms out around 20 ft (6 m) with a submerged platform used for skills practice; a funnel-shaped opening mid-basin leads to a cave bottoming out at 45-50 ft (13.5-15 m). Cave entry is for cave-experienced divers only. Visibility is strongly influenced by the nearby Choctawhatchee River and drops when the river runs above 5 ft (1.5 m). Fishing boats share the basin via a boat ramp, so dive flags are required.
